title: Venturo Host Terms Agreement
summary: These Host Terms and Conditions apply when a Host registers, lists or manages an Event through Venturo.

blocks.text: These Host Terms and Conditions (“Terms”) apply when a Host registers, lists or manages an Event through the Venturo website, application or another Venturo service (“Platform”).

The default payment arrangement for independent Hosts is direct payment: Customers book and pay the Host, and Venturo does not collect, hold, manage or distribute those booking funds. The payout and payment-hold terms in these Terms apply only when Venturo expressly activates checkout and payout for a specific Event.
1. Key terms
Event means a ticketed activity, experience or gathering listed by a Host on the Platform.
Customer means a person who buys, or tries to buy, a ticket or booking for an Event.
Host means the event organiser or service provider that submits or manages an Event through the Platform.
Payment Provider means the bank, acquirer or payment service engaged to process or settle a transaction.

Venturo-enabled checkout and payout means an arrangement for a specific Host and Event for which Venturo has approved Platform checkout, a Payment Provider and a payout route in the Host account or in a separate written confirmation.
Working Day means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday observed in South Africa.
2. Host responsibilities
The Host is responsible for organising and supplying its Event. The Host must identify itself clearly to Customers before purchase, including its legal or trading name and a working contact channel.

The Host must provide accurate information, keep its listings current, honour the advertised ticket price and capacity, admit Customers with valid tickets, and deliver each Event at the advertised time and place in a manner and quality Customers may reasonably expect.
The Host must not materially change, oversell, substitute or cancel an Event without promptly notifying Venturo and affected Customers and offering the remedies required by law.

The Host must retain reliable attendance, ticket-scan, cancellation, refund and customer-communication records for each Event. It must provide relevant records to Venturo on request to resolve a complaint, payment dispute or investigation.

Venturo may display approved Event listings. It does not become the organiser or supplier of a Host’s Event merely because the Event appears on the Platform. Venturo-operated Events are supplied and sold by Venturo and are outside the Host payout arrangements in these Terms.
The parties’ legal responsibilities to Customers depend on the transaction and applicable law. Nothing in these Terms removes a duty or liability that the law does not allow a party to exclude.
3. Event listings and delivery
Before tickets go on sale, the Host must provide complete, accurate and current information, including:
the Event name, description, date, start and end times, venue and access instructions;
the Host’s identity and contact details, ticket types, capacity, total price and any mandatory charges or taxes;
age limits, accessibility information, material eligibility rules and equipment requirements; and
cancellation or refund terms, material risks, restrictions, schedule changes and other conditions a Customer needs before deciding to book.

The Host must ensure that the listing remains accurate and that the Event is delivered substantially as advertised. The Host must promptly notify Venturo and affected Customers of any material change, postponement or cancellation.
The Host must provide any attendance or delivery evidence reasonably needed to confirm that the Event took place and was delivered substantially as advertised.
4. Legal compliance, permits and safety

The Host is responsible for securing and maintaining all permissions, licences, venue approvals, insurance and qualified personnel reasonably required to run the Event lawfully and safely. The Host must follow applicable health, safety, fire, alcohol, food, accessibility, child-protection and municipal requirements, as relevant to the Event.

The Host must assess foreseeable risks, use suitable safeguards and give Customers clear, prominent information about material or unusual risks before purchase and again before participation where appropriate. A risk notice must not ask a Customer to waive a right or liability that cannot lawfully be waived.
The Host must immediately tell Venturo about any serious safety incident, regulator or venue action, loss of required permission, or circumstance that may prevent safe delivery.
5. Customer information and consumer rights

The Host must ensure that information shown before checkout is plain, complete and consistent with the Event as delivered. Customer prices and compulsory charges must be shown before the Customer pays. The Host’s cancellation terms must be visible before purchase, fair in the circumstances and consistent with the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008 (“CPA”) and any other applicable law.

Where CPA section 17 applies, a Customer may cancel an advance booking and any cancellation charge must be reasonable in the circumstances. A cancellation fee may not be charged where the Act prohibits it, including where the Customer is unable to honour the booking because the person for whose benefit it was made has died or been hospitalised. Any applicable exclusion from an online cooling-off right for a leisure service on a specific date does not remove other consumer rights.

The Host must provide timely performance, give notice of unavoidable delay and address service-quality failures with the remedy required by law. This may include correcting the failure or refunding a reasonable portion of the price.

No term of these Terms or of a Host’s Customer policy may waive a Customer’s statutory rights, exclude liability for gross negligence where prohibited, or prevent a Customer from raising a genuine complaint.
6. Cancellations, complaints and refunds

If the Host cancels an Event, fails to hold it or cannot provide the material service paid for, the Host must notify Venturo immediately, stop further sales and cooperate in giving affected Customers the refund, alternative date or other remedy required by law.

For a cancelled or unprovided Event, the Host must fund a full refund of the amount paid for the affected booking. If an Event is postponed, Customers must be told the new date and given any choice or refund required by law. If an Event is partly delivered or materially differs from its listing, the Host must provide the remedy required by applicable consumer law, including a reasonable partial refund where appropriate.

For an Event with Venturo-enabled checkout and payout, Venturo may submit an authorised or legally required refund through the approved Payment Provider against the Host’s unpaid proceeds. If those proceeds are insufficient, the Host must reimburse Venturo within five Working Days after receiving an itemised statement of the amount and reason.

For a direct-to-Host payment, the Host must process any refund itself. Venturo cannot refund money it did not receive. The Host may not substitute a credit or voucher where the Customer is legally entitled to a refund.
Venturo’s Refund & Cancellation Policy applies to purchases made directly from Venturo. It does not turn a direct-to-Host booking into a Venturo payment.

The Host must respond to a customer complaint referred by Venturo within five Working Days, provide relevant evidence and cooperate in a fair investigation. Venturo may communicate directly with a Customer, request further information from the Host or Payment Provider, and decide whether a transaction should be refunded or reversed where required by law, the published Customer terms or reliable evidence. The Host must not retaliate against or pressure a Customer for making a complaint.
7. Payment arrangements and customer funds

For most independent Host Events, Customers book and pay the Host directly. The Host or its own payment provider receives and processes those payments. Venturo does not collect, hold, manage or distribute direct-to-Host booking funds.

A Host may use Venturo-enabled checkout and payout only after Venturo confirms the arrangement for the specific Event. The Host authorises Venturo to facilitate payment through the approved Payment Provider and account for ticket receipts, deductions, refunds, reversals and payouts in an Event statement. The approved Provider and settlement route will be recorded in the Host account or confirmed separately before sales begin.

Paystack is currently used for payments for services supplied directly by Venturo. It may be used for Host payouts only if Venturo separately confirms that the Provider and account configuration support that arrangement.

Where CPA section 64 applies to a payment made more than 25 Working Days before the service is to be provided, the money remains the Customer’s property until it may lawfully be charged. Neither Venturo nor the Host may treat those funds as earned Host proceeds or pay them out before performance except as permitted by law.

Each party that holds money or property belonging to a Customer must handle it with the care required by law. These Terms do not represent that funds are kept in a trust account or escrow unless Venturo separately confirms that arrangement in writing.

The Host must provide the transaction and supplier details needed for a compliant Customer receipt or record, including its legal name, service description, price, tax information and service location. The Host must promptly report suspected payment fraud, duplicate charges or unauthorised use of its account. The Host must retain its own records for direct-to-Host payments.
8. Event-specific payment details
For each Event, the Host account or Event setup flow must show the payment mode and, where Venturo-enabled checkout and payout is approved:
the Event and its activation status;
the Customer-facing supplier identity and refund contact;
the approved Payment Provider and settlement route;
any Venturo commission, listing fee or processing fee, and who pays it;
any other agreed deduction; and
the Host’s verified payout account and applicable payout timing.

The payment mode, supplier identity, Payment Provider and refund contact shown to Customers must match the actual transaction. Direct payment to the Host is the default unless Venturo confirms Venturo-enabled checkout and payout for that Event.
9. Payout timing and statements
For an Event with Venturo-enabled checkout and payout and no active hold, Venturo will instruct payment of the Host’s net proceeds within two Working Days after the Event ends.

If the approved Payment Provider has not released cleared funds by then, Venturo will instruct payment within two Working Days after those funds clear and will notify the Host of the delay. For a multi-session Event, settlement may occur after each session or after the final session, as recorded in the Host account or Event setup flow. No Venturo payout is due for a direct-to-Host payment.

Net proceeds are ticket payments actually received, less only fees and amounts disclosed and accepted before sale, customer refunds and reversals, chargebacks, taxes required by law, and a hold allowed by clause 10. Venturo will provide an itemised statement showing the calculation.
The Host must dispute a statement with supporting detail within 30 calendar days after it is provided. This does not limit a right that cannot lawfully be limited.

Payouts will be sent to the verified account recorded in the Host account. The Host is responsible for correct account details and any resulting bank charge or delay, except to the extent caused by Venturo. Venturo may require identity, business or bank verification before the first payout or when details change.
10. Temporary payout holds and investigations
Only for an Event with Venturo-enabled checkout and payout, Venturo may temporarily hold the payout, or a reasonable part of it, where:
a Customer complaint remains unresolved and reasonably concerns non-delivery, a material difference from the listing, a safety issue, a refund or a payment dispute;
there are reasonable grounds to investigate whether the Event occurred or was delivered substantially as advertised; or
a Payment Provider, card scheme, bank, court or regulator requires or permits a reserve, reversal or delay.

An investigation may take account of attendance or venue records, ticket scans, Customer reports, communications, photographs or other reliable evidence. A complaint or investigation alone is not a finding of wrongdoing.

Where reasonably practicable and lawful, Venturo will notify the Host within two Working Days after placing a hold, explain its basis and scope, and identify what information is needed. The Host will have at least five Working Days to respond.

A hold must be proportionate to the reasonably foreseeable refund, reversal or loss exposure. Venturo may hold all unpaid proceeds for that Event where credible evidence raises an Event-wide concern, including that the Event did not take place. Venturo will release any undisputed balance promptly and review an ongoing hold at least every ten Working Days. If more time is reasonably needed, Venturo will tell the Host why and provide a further review date.

When the complaint or investigation is resolved, Venturo will, within two Working Days, release the balance due or apply the amount reasonably required to customer refunds, reversals or other sums properly payable under these Terms.

If the evidence establishes that the Event did not occur or was materially not delivered, Venturo may first use the held proceeds to refund affected Customers and then provide the Host with an itemised account. A hold does not remove any Customer remedy or the Host’s obligation to fund refunds that exceed held proceeds.
For direct-to-Host payments, Venturo cannot withhold funds it does not hold. The Host remains responsible for resolving the complaint and providing any refund.
11. Fees, tax and deductions

Venturo may charge only the commission, listing, processing or other fees shown in the Host account or Event setup flow and accepted before the relevant tickets go on sale. No new fee applies retroactively to a completed sale.

For a direct-to-Host payment, Venturo does not deduct a commission or process a payout from the Customer’s booking funds. Each party is responsible for its own income tax and tax registrations. The Host must give Venturo accurate VAT details, if registered, and set prices and tax information in the manner required by law.

For an Event with Venturo-enabled checkout and payout, Venturo may set off against amounts otherwise payable to the Host any refund, reversal, chargeback, fee, tax or other amount due under these Terms, provided the item is identified in the Event statement. This does not authorise Venturo to debit or withhold a direct-to-Host Customer payment. The Host remains liable for a verified shortfall after set-off.
12. Personal information
Each party must handle Customer and Host personal information in accordance with the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (“POPIA”) and applicable privacy notices.

The Host may use Customer information received through Venturo only to administer the booking, deliver the Event, meet legal obligations and resolve customer service issues. The Host may not add Customers to marketing lists or share their information for unrelated purposes without a lawful basis and any required consent.

The Host must use reasonable security safeguards, limit access to people who need the information, keep it only as long as needed or legally required, and promptly notify Venturo of a suspected loss, unauthorised access or disclosure involving Platform Customer information. The Host must cooperate with reasonable requests to correct, delete or protect personal information.
13. Content and promotional permission

The Host grants Venturo a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence during the time the Host uses the Platform to host, reproduce, display, adapt for format and promote the Host’s approved Event name, description, logo, photographs and other submitted materials for operating and marketing the Event and Platform.

The Host confirms it has the rights and permissions needed to grant this licence and that its materials do not infringe another person’s rights. Venturo may remove or correct content that is unlawful, misleading, unsafe or inconsistent with these Terms.
14. Responsibility and claims between the parties
The Host is responsible for the Event, its personnel and venue arrangements, and for claims arising from the Host’s breach, negligence, unlawful conduct or failure to deliver as advertised.

To the extent permitted by law, the Host must reimburse Venturo for reasonable, documented losses and costs directly caused by that conduct, including refunds and payment reversals. This obligation does not apply to the extent a loss was caused by Venturo’s own breach, negligence or unlawful conduct.

Neither party limits or excludes liability where the law does not permit it. Neither party is liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss except to the extent arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality or privacy, or a payment or refund obligation under these Terms.
Nothing in this clause affects a Customer’s rights against any supplier or intermediary under applicable law.
15. Suspension, termination and notices

Venturo may pause new sales or suspend an Event where reasonably necessary to address a safety, legal, fraud, consumer-protection or payment risk, or a material breach by the Host. Where practicable, Venturo will give notice and an opportunity to respond. Venturo may remove an Event immediately where continued sale creates an urgent risk.

The Host may stop using the Platform and end its Host account by giving notice through the account or to Venturo. Venturo may terminate the Host’s access for a material breach that is not remedied within ten Working Days after written notice, or immediately where the breach cannot reasonably be remedied.

Ending access does not cancel a Customer’s existing booking or remove the Host’s responsibility to deliver, refund or support it. These Terms continue to apply as needed to complete existing transactions and resolve related obligations.

The Host should send listing, Event and partnership notices to business@venturo.co.za and payout or payment notices to billing@venturo.co.za. Formal notices to Venturo may be sent to legal@venturo.co.za. Venturo will use the Host contact details in its account for notices to the Host, so the Host must keep them current.
16. Disputes and governing law
The parties will first try in good faith to resolve a dispute through their designated contacts. If unresolved, either party may use any available mediation, ombud, tribunal or court process.

These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of South Africa, and the courts with jurisdiction in South Africa may hear disputes. This clause does not restrict a Customer’s statutory complaint or redress rights.
17. General terms

These Terms govern Host registrations, Platform Event listings, Event delivery and any Venturo-enabled checkout and payout arrangement. A specific payment or fee arrangement applies only when it is shown in the Host account or Event setup flow and accepted before the relevant tickets go on sale.

If an Event-specific commercial term conflicts with these Terms, these Terms apply unless Venturo and the Host clearly agree in writing that the Event term overrides them. If any provision is unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue to apply, and the provision must be read as narrowly as necessary to make it lawful. A failure to enforce a provision immediately is not a waiver.

The Host may not transfer its account or obligations without Venturo’s written consent. Venturo may use service providers to operate the Platform and process payments, while remaining responsible for its own obligations under law.
